review_mode: Scheduled cloud dual-review; independent Codex desk
limitations: Confidence values are subjective evidence confidence, not return probabilities. News remains unweighted in the trading score.

The material change since the 09:45 Codex review is a deterioration in near-term Middle East de-escalation odds. Same-session Refinery, Oil Marketing and Banking ratings are carried forward because their underlying evidence remains current and no contradictory material update was found.

The committed Business Recorder Iran link was not retrievable as a full page in the cloud browser, so that raw item was treated as headline-only evidence. The same reported refusal to negotiate was verified in a full Aaj article. The committed Mettis oil item's raw timestamp appeared future relative to its fetch when interpreted literally, so that raw timestamp was not used as a verified publication time.

A generic electricity power-sector regulatory story was verified as irrelevant to POWER, which is Power Cement; it did not create a POWER rating. The 10:08 Mettis banking item restated the same SBP H1CY26 review already rated earlier rather than creating a new banking call.
Stories not reviewed are not Neutral ratings.

market_context.topic: Middle East oil supply shock and stalled diplomacy
market_context.impact: Negative for the broad market, positive for upstream oil exposure
market_context.reason: The existing Saudi pipeline and Hormuz supply disruption is now paired with an explicit Iranian rejection of US talks until Tehran's conditions are met. That lowers near-term de-escalation odds, increasing the risk that elevated crude continues to pressure Pakistan's import bill and inflation while supporting upstream oil-linked revenues.
SBP reserves reached about $21.4bn after Eurobond inflows and FX purchases, improving the external buffer. Part of the increase is debt-funded and does not remove the oil-shock risk.
